# Accuracy and Limitations

## Theoretical Foundation

The exact static call graph is an undecidable problem [6][7]. By Rice's theorem,
no algorithm can be both sound (no false negatives) and complete (no false
positives) for call graph construction in a Turing-complete language [7]. All
static call graph algorithms are therefore overapproximations [6].

For Python specifically, "without full type inference, accurate call-graphs are
impossible" [5]. A complete call graph is "much harder than [a] complete
control-flow graph" because higher-order functions make it "nearly impossible"
to determine which functions will execute [5].

Static dead-code detection in Python is undecidable in the general case — "not
'hard', not 'tricky' — undecidable" [56].

## Python Constructs That Break Static Call Graphs

| Construct | Why It Breaks | Example |
|-----------|--------------|---------|
| Dynamic dispatch (getattr) [56] | Target resolved from runtime string | `getattr(obj, name)()` |
| Duck typing [56] | No type info for method resolution | `obj.process()` |
| Import-by-string [56] | No syntactic import statement | Django `INSTALLED_APPS` |
| Metaclasses [56] | Rewrite class bodies at runtime | `class Meta(type): ...` |
| Decorators [47] | Modify function behavior invisibly | `@app.route("/")` |
| Monkey patching [56] | Runtime dict mutation | `module.func = other_func` |
| Dynamic code execution [56] | Arbitrary runtime code | String-based execution |
| C extensions [5] | Opaque to Python analysis | `numpy` internals |
| Higher-order functions [5] | Function identity unknown | `def f(x): x(1)` |
| Framework control flow [63] | Implicit hook invocation | Flask/Django lifecycle |

Frameworks are a particular challenge: Flask and Django have "obfuscated control
flows" where the framework determines execution order with "no explicit calls to
hooks" visible in source code [63].

## Measured Accuracy

| Tool | Precision | Recall | Benchmark | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|-----------|--------|
| PyCG | ~99.2% | ~69.9% | 112 micro-programs | [1] |
| JARVIS | 84% higher than PyCG | at least 20% higher than PyCG | 135 micro + 6 macro | [2] |
| Pyan | Average | Low (7.6% on some tests) | 112 micro-programs | [9] |
| Depends | 98.7% | 14.4% | 112 micro-programs | [9] |
| JVM bytecode conversion | N/A | N/A | N/A | >96% false positives [1] |

PyCG achieves 99.2% precision on micro-benchmarks but fails completely on 4 of
6 real-world applications (24-hour timeout, recursion errors, OOM) [2]. The gap
between micro-benchmark and real-world performance is severe.

## The Precision-Recall Trade-off

Tools must choose between:

- **High precision, low recall** (Depends: 98.7% / 14.4%): Only report calls
  you are certain about. Misses 85% of actual calls [9].
- **High precision, moderate recall** (PyCG: 99.2% / 69.9%): Broader coverage
  but still misses 30% of calls [1].
- **Flow-sensitive improvement** (JARVIS): Better on both axes via type graphs,
  but at the cost of complexity [2].

No tool achieves both high precision and high recall. This is not an
implementation gap — it is a theoretical impossibility [7].

## Dynamic Analysis Accuracy

Dynamic tools produce no false positives for executed paths (they trace what
actually happened) [6] but:

- Miss all paths not executed during the trace session [6]
- sys.settrace overhead (10x+) distorts the behavior being traced [59]
- Python 3.12 worsened this: 7x overhead vs 3.11's 3x for the same workload
  [59]
- Sampling profilers (py-spy, ~1%) sacrifice completeness for accuracy [21]

## IDE Accuracy

IDE call hierarchies (Pylance, PyCharm) do not publish accuracy metrics.
Documented failures include:

- Complete failure for aliased imports [41]
- Wrong results for overridden methods [43]
- No disambiguation for same-name methods across classes [42]

These are acknowledged limitations, not bugs — some are marked "by design" [41].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No standardized benchmark exists for Python call graph accuracy — PyCG uses
  112 programs, JARVIS uses 135, DyPyBench uses 50 real projects [1][2].
- C extension handling is undocumented across all tools.
- No tool measures accuracy on framework-heavy code (Django, Flask) despite
  frameworks being the #1 source of dynamic control flow in Python [63].
- The gap between micro-benchmark accuracy (99.2%) and real-world failure
  (4/6 timeouts) suggests published precision/recall numbers may be
  misleading [1][2].
